Simulate example input data

Source: R/example-data.R
example_scaleup_data.Rd

Generates a fabricated firm-level panel in the format of the input files (see vignette("input-data") and vignette("input-trade-data")), large enough for every part of the package to produce output: firms that enter and exit, high-growth episodes, a few firms that grow past 250 employees, plants, exports and imports. Used in vignette("OECDscaleup"); useful to try the package without confidential data.

Usage

example_scaleup_data(n_firms = 3000, years = 2010:2022, seed = 1)

Arguments

n_firms

Number of firms.

years

Calendar years of the panel (consecutive).

seed

Random seed; the same seed gives the same data. The global random number stream is left as it was.

Value

A list of three data frames:

  • base_financials: one row per firm and year (idf, year, birth_year, sector, region, employment and the financial variables, independent, uco, exit_acq); money in EUR thousand;

  • plants_raw: one row per plant and year (idf, idp, year);

  • trade_raw: one row per firm, year, flow, destination and product (idf, year, trade_type, trade_value, code_destin, prod_code).

Details

The data are random and mean nothing: the sizes, growth rates and ratios are only roughly plausible. The country is France ("FR"), so the region codes are real French NUTS codes that link to tl3_typology.

Examples

ex <- example_scaleup_data(n_firms = 200)
sapply(ex, nrow)
#> base_financials      plants_raw       trade_raw 
#>            1614            2181            3199
